title: Latency vs Throughput
subtitle: Batching buys capacity with waiting, so pick the smallest batch that keeps up
motto: Batch until you keep up, and not one item further
keyInsight: One item at a time gives the lowest latency but cannot keep up once fixed costs dominate, and a batch larger than needed only adds waiting, so the right size is the smallest one with enough capacity.

decisions.title: Output the smallest sufficient batch
decisions.description: The last frame searches for the smallest batch whose capacity covers the arrivals plus headroom, so the answer is a number to compare against a latency target.
decisions.alternatives: Reporting only 'small is fast, large is efficient' would leave the reader to guess where between.

decisions.title: Show both extremes failing
decisions.description: One item at a time fails on capacity and a huge batch fails on latency, so neither pure choice is presented as the safe one.
decisions.alternatives: Showing only the batch that fails the target would make batching look bad.
